extracted.intended_audience: grant reviewers and gene-therapy researchers (molecular virologists working on AAV vectors)
extracted.subtask_description: A preclinical research strategy for designing and evaluating AAV vectors that enhance human liver transduction while minimizing capsid antigen presentation and CTL-mediated clearance, using mutant capsids, pharmacologic modulators, and humanized/xenograft mouse models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess capsid antigen presentation from AAV empty particles in vivo (kinetics and dose-response)
rubrics_metrics.description: Study the kinetics and dose-response of AAV capsid antigen presentation from AAV empty virions in vivo.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administer empty and full particles (AAV2-OVA and AAV8-OVA) at defined doses and time points; transfuse CFSE-labeled OT-1 spleen cells and measure CD8+ OT-1 proliferation ten days after transfer as a readout of OVA epitope presentation. Use CsCl gradient-purified empty particles and titer via Western blot (A20/ADK8). Expected kinetics: early cross-presentation (days 3–12, 21–30) with waning by later time points; test doses from 10^8–10^12 particles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determine effect of empty particles on antigen presentation and transgene production from full particles
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate how co-administration (various empty:full ratios) of empty capsids affects transgene expression from full AAV particles and capsid antigen presentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Spike 1×10^11 full AAV/AAT with increasing empty capsid amounts (0 to 1×10^12) and measure AAT concentrations in blood at weeks 1,2,4,6 (ELISA). For antigen presentation, infuse CFSE-labeled OT-1 cells three days post-injection and assay proliferation. Also test the reciprocal (full particles spiked into empty virion preparations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use genetic knockout models to distinguish antigen presentation pathways (TAP-/- vs Cat S-/-)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use TAP-deficient and Cathepsin S-deficient mice to determine whether capsid antigen presentation from empty or full AAV particles proceeds via TAP-dependent (cytosolic/proteasome) vs endocytic protease-dependent pathways.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inject AAV-OVA into TAP-/-, Cat S-/-, and wild-type C57BL mice, measure transgene (AAT ELISA) and perform in vivo OT-1 proliferation assays (transfer 5×10^6 CFSE-labeled OT-1 cells three days post-injection; analyze ten days later). Anticipate that comparable or lower presentation in TAP-/- mice would implicate endocytic/cytosolic contributions; use proteasome inhibitors if necessary to probe proteasome role.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigate effects of AAV capsid mutants and proteasome inhibitors on capsid antigen cross-presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether capsid genetic modifications and pharmacologic enhancers (e.g., proteasome inhibitors) that increase liver transduction also alter capsid antigen presentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test mutants (AAV2G9, AAV2D, AAV2D/585E, AAV2i8, AAV2i8G9, etc.) and proteasome inhibitors (MG132, bortezomib, carfilzomib) in vivo and in vitro; measure transgene expression (luciferase imaging, AAT ELISA) and antigen presentation (OT-1 proliferation). Account for dose-dependent drug effects (high-dose bortezomib may block presentation; low-dose may increase it), drug toxicity, short half-life (peak ~30 min), and use highest non-lethal repeated dosing with short-interval analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Isolate AAV chimeric capsids with human hepatocyte tropism and CTL evasion
rubrics_metrics.description: Use directed evolution combined with rational capsid design (e.g., mutations to avoid ubiquitination) in human hepatocyte xenograft mice to select mutants with enhanced human liver transduction and reduced capsid antigen display to CTLs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recover mutants from humanized mice, verify human liver transduction efficiency in xenograft models (e.g., measure transgene expression), characterize sequences/phenotypes of recovered mutants, and test capsid CTL evasion (reduced OT-1/proliferative or CTL killing assays). Aim for mutants that escape ubiquitination/degradation so they present less capsid-derived peptide on target cells and can be used even in presence of pre-existing cellular immunity (note: NAb presence prevents study of capsid presentation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrate proteasome dependence of capsid antigen presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Show that capsid antigen presentation relies on proteasome-mediated degradation of the AAV capsid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use proteasome inhibitors (MG132, bortezomib) in vitro and in vivo: inhibitors enhance transduction but can abolish OVA antigen presentation (in vitro); combine with Brefeldin A and endosomal inhibitors (ammonium chloride, chloroquine) to map trafficking (Brefeldin A suppresses transduction and presentation; endosomal acidification inhibitors block transduction and >90% of presentation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify dose-thresholds for capsid-driven T cell stimulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Define the vector dose threshold required to elicit efficient CD8+ T cell stimulation in vivo.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observed stimulation: 5×10^10 AAV2-OVA particles induced OT-1 proliferation, whereas doses ≤1×10^10 did not. Use CFSE-labeled OT-1 transfer assays and proliferation index as quantitative readouts; plan dose-escalation experiments across 10^8–10^12 particles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design capsid modifications to increase transduction while modulating immunogenicity
rubrics_metrics.description: Modify capsid receptor-binding or ubiquitination sites (e.g., tyrosine residue mutations, insertion at residue 265, engraftment of Gal footprint) to increase liver transduction and potentially reduce capsid antigen presentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: engraft AAV9 galactose-binding residues into AAV2 (AAV2G9) to increase liver expression, mutate tyrosines to avoid ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation (improves nuclear trafficking and reduces CTL elimination), and test tissue tropism shifts (AAV2i8, AAV2D, AAV2/585E). Measure luciferase activity and AAT levels; compare immune elimination markers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for purification method limitations (empty particle contamination)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that ion-exchange chromatography (scalable) cannot separate empty from genome-containing particles and that empty particle contamination can inhibit transduction and increase capsid antigen load.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use CsCl density gradient purification where separation of full vs empty is required for mechanistic studies; quantify empty particles and monitor their impact on transduction and antigen presentation in experimental designs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use appropriate quantitative readouts for transgene and antigen presentation endpoints
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ validated assays for both therapeutic transgene expression and capsid antigen presentation to evaluate effects of mutants/drugs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transgene: AAT ELISA (blood timecourse at weeks 1,2,4,6) and in vivo luciferase imaging. Antigen presentation: OT-1 CFSE-labeled T cell proliferation assays (spleen/liver harvest, CD8/CD69 staining, proliferation index). Include representative flow cytometry histograms and compute means ± standard error.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical analysis standardization
rubrics_metrics.description: Present and analyze data using consistent statistical methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Express data as means ± standard error and determine significance with Student's t-test (software example: StatView, SAS). Report p-values and mark significance levels (e.g., *p<0.05, **p<0.01). Use replicate groups (e.g., four mice per group) for in vivo assays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Probe intracellular trafficking and uncoating determinants of antigen presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Test the role of endosomal escape (PLA2 domain) and nuclear localization signals (NLSs BR1/BR2/BR3) in capsid antigen presentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use AAV2-OVA/75HD/AN (PLA2 mutant) and VP3-only virus to show decreased antigen presentation due to impaired endosomal escape. Test NLS mutants: BR1 mutation reduces presentation while BR2/BR3 mutants may not, suggesting nuclear uncoating is not required for antigen presentation. Combine with chemical inhibitors to interpret trafficking contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan for anticipated results, pitfalls, and alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Anticipate possible outcomes (e.g., empty particle effects, TAP independence, proteasome inhibitor toxicity) and outline alternative approaches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect empty virion presentation to be dose-dependent and early; high empty contamination likely inhibits full-particle transgene production and may enhance antigen presentation. If TAP-/- mice still show presentation, consider proteasome dependence and test proteasome inhibitors in vivo. Use fluorescence-labeled virions to track trafficking and adjust dosing/schedules to mitigate drug toxicity and pharmacokinetics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider species- and model-specific translatability
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that mouse transduction does not always predict human hepatocyte transduction and that model selection is critical for clinical relevance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use human hepatocyte xenografted (humanized) mouse models for selecting mutants intended for human liver targeting; verify that mutants recovered from humanized mice have enhanced human hepatocyte tropism before clinical translation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optimize proteasome inhibitor dosing to balance transduction enhancement and antigen presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Design inhibitor dosing regimens mindful that high doses can block presentation while low doses may paradoxically increase antigen presentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Given toxicity and short half-life of inhibitors like bortezomib, use the highest non-lethal dose with repeated delivery (three days) and analyze antigen presentation over a short window after CD8 cell infusion. Monitor for enhancement of antigen presentation at low doses and plan dose-response studies to identify safe/effective regimens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use pharmacological inhibitors as mechanistic probes
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply endosomal acidification inhibitors, protease inhibitors, proteasome inhibitors, and secretory pathway blockers to map antigen-processing steps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: ammonium chloride and chloroquine inhibit endosomal acidification and block >90% of antigen presentation; leupeptin and pepstatin A partially block presentation (proteases); MG132 and bortezomib eliminate OVA presentation (proteasome); Brefeldin A suppresses presentation (blocks Golgi-mediated transport). Use non-toxic concentrations and timed pre-incubation protocols.
